Class PluginResolver

java.lang.Object
com.erudika.para.core.utils.PluginResolver
public final class PluginResolver extends Object
Downloads Para plugins and their runtime dependencies from Maven Central into the plugin folder.

Plugins are published as thin JARs. Each one carries a precomputed list of its runtime dependencies in META-INF/para/plugin-deps.txt, generated at build time by maven-dependency-plugin:list. This class fetches a plugin JAR, reads that manifest without executing anything, then downloads each listed artifact into the plugin folder where Para.getParaClassLoader() can see it.

Every downloaded artifact is checksum-verified before it is moved into place. SHA-256 is preferred, SHA-1 is accepted as a fallback for artifacts that predate SHA-256 publication, and a download is discarded if neither digest is available. Files are written to a temporary location and atomically renamed, so a partial or corrupt download can never become visible to the classloader.

The plugin folder is a flat classpath, so at most one version of any given library is kept. When two plugins disagree about a version, the higher one wins and the lower one is removed. This keeps the classpath deterministic regardless of the order plugins were installed in.

Version conflicts are resolved per artifact, not per library. Installing para-search-lucene after para-search-elasticsearch therefore leaves the Lucene modules that only Elasticsearch needs at the version Elasticsearch asked for, and upgrades only the modules both plugins declare. For the official plugins this means Lucene patch versions can coexist, which is safe because a patch release of the same Lucene minor version is binary compatible.

  • Method Details

    • resolvePlugin

      public PluginResolver.ResolutionResult resolvePlugin(String groupId, String artifactId, String version) throws IOException
      Downloads a plugin and all of its runtime dependencies into the plugin folder.

      This is the bootstrap sequence: the plugin JAR is fetched first, then its embedded manifest is read as a ZIP entry (no classloading, no code execution), then each listed dependency is fetched and verified. The plugin is not usable until this method returns without error, and a restart is required before the plugin can be loaded.

      Parameters:
      groupId - the Maven groupId of the plugin
      artifactId - the Maven artifactId of the plugin
      version - the plugin version
      Returns:
      a result describing what was downloaded and what was already present
      Throws:
      IOException - if the plugin cannot be fetched, its manifest is missing or unreadable, or any artifact fails checksum verification
